exitProficiencyTarget: Novice Mid, stretch Novice High by grade 5
standardsBasis: Program-design target per expansion-plan-2026-09 §3 B1 (no WA K-8 benchmark exists; ACTFL research anchors Novice Mid; STAMP 4Se is WA's named assessment for grades 3-6). Standard tags use WA's 2015 World Languages standard numbers (5 Cs). Sub-standard numbering verified 2026-09-05 against the primary source (OSPI v1.3 PDF, p.6, "II. World Languages Learning Standards"): 1.1 Interpersonal/1.2 Interpretive/1.3 Presentational Communication; 2.1 Relating Cultural Practices/2.2 Relating Cultural Products to Perspectives; 3.1 Making Connections/3.2 Acquiring Information and Diverse Perspectives; 4.1 Language/4.2 Cultural Comparisons; 5.1 School and Global Communities/5.2 Lifelong Learning.
bandNotes: Literacy comes online this band: children read and copy words and sentence frames, but listening/speaking still lead every week. Grammar is taught as memorized frames (soy, tengo, me gusta, está), never as conjugation tables. By week 36 students produce memorized-plus-slightly-adapted sentences and lists — Novice Mid, with grade-5 students stretching toward strung-together original sentences (Novice High). Assumes no prior Spanish (entry point for new families); K-2 vocabulary reappears inside richer frames rather than being presumed.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — greeting people at different times of day
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Greeting rotations — clock pictures cue buenos días/tardes/noches; first copy of the words into the Spanish notebook.
Day 2: '¿Cómo estás?' dialogue chain with feeling faces; practice muy bien/mal responses.
Day 3: Meet-and-greet speed rounds ending in mucho gusto with a handshake.
Day 4: Read a short illustrated greeting comic; match speech bubbles to pictures.
Day 5: Perform a 4-line greeting skit in pairs; class listens for each courtesy phrase.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — exchanging names and where you're from
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Name-exchange dialogues; write your own 'Me llamo ___' name tent.
Day 2: Introduce a partner — 'Se llama...' third-person practice.
Day 3: '¿De dónde eres?' with a world map — students mark where family is from.
Day 4: Señor/señora courtesy practice — greeting adults vs. friends.
Day 5: Passport day — complete a paper passport (name, from) and interview three classmates.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Language Comparisons — Spanish letters and sounds vs. English (ñ, rr, silent h)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Alphabet song; spot which letters look the same but sound different from English.
Day 2: Vowel bootcamp — the five pure vowel sounds; vowel-sound bingo.
Day 3: Special sounds day — ñ, rr, ll, silent h; tongue-twister play (perro/pero).
Day 4: '¿Cómo se escribe?' spelling exchanges with classmates' names.
Day 5: Spelling bee lite — spell familiar words aloud in Spanish letter names.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — counting and simple math in Spanish
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Count 0-30 with a rhythm pattern; write the tricky teens.
Day 2: Number dictation — hear it, write the numeral.
Day 3: Math-fact races in Spanish — 'dos más tres son...' addition aloud.
Day 4: Real-world numbers — phone-number and lunch-count practice.
Day 5: Number bingo 0-30 with student callers.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — understanding larger numbers by tens
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Tens chant 10-100; build numbers with tens + ones cards.
Day 2: Number listening grid — circle the number you hear (47 vs. 74 traps).
Day 3: Guess-my-number game with más/menos clues.
Day 4: Prices and quantities — count play money to 100.
Day 5: 100-chart challenge — teacher calls, students race to cover the square.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — following classroom commands and naming supplies
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Classroom scavenger hunt — label real objects with word cards.
Day 2: Classroom commands TPR — saquen el cuaderno, escuchen, levanten la mano.
Day 3: 'What's on my desk?' memory game with supplies.
Day 4: Read and follow a 4-step written instruction card (draw, write, cut).
Day 5: Student teachers give the class supply commands.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — describing objects by color and quality
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Rapid color review (all 11 color words), then add claro/oscuro shades.
Day 2: Paint-chip sorting — azul claro vs. azul oscuro; noun + adjective word order.
Day 3: Describe mystery objects — 'Es rojo y brillante. ¿Qué es?'
Day 4: Write three sentences describing favorite objects, using es + color + adjective.
Day 5: Art-gallery walk — present a colored drawing: 'Mi arcoíris es bonito.'

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — reading a calendar and dates in Spanish
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Days-of-week review chant; learn all twelve month names with a calendar march.
Day 2: Date format detective — in Spanish the day comes first (el 4 de septiembre); write today's fecha.
Day 3: Birthday line-up — order yourselves by month, say your month aloud.
Day 4: Read a real Spanish-language calendar page; find holidays and weekends.
Day 5: Class calendar build — each student writes one event with its fecha.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — delivering a simple weather report
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Weather-phrase review + new expressions; weather-map symbols matching.
Day 2: Listen to a kid-level weather forecast; circle what you hear.
Day 3: Compare Seattle weather to a Latin American city's weather this week.
Day 4: Script a two-line weather report with a partner and rehearse.
Day 5: Weather-anchor day — present reports at the map like TV meteorologists.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — extended family life in Latin America
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Family-tree vocabulary with a big class tree; place each label.
Day 2: Draw and label your own family tree (chosen family welcome).
Day 3: Learn how many Latin American families share homes with abuelos and celebrate with primos; compare with your own family gatherings.
Day 4: 'Who is it?' riddles — 'Es la hermana de mi papá' (la tía).
Day 5: Present your family tree in 3-4 sentences to a small group.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — describing yourself and others
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Soy/es frames — 'Soy alta. Mi papá es alto.' Notice the o/a endings.
Day 2: Describe storybook characters with adjective cards.
Day 3: Hair and eyes — 'Tiene el pelo café' guessing game about classmates (kindly).
Day 4: Write a 4-sentence self-description paragraph with a self-portrait.
Day 5: Mystery-person read-alouds — class guesses who each paragraph describes.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — daily feelings check-ins
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Estoy/estás frames with emotion cards; upgrade the morning check-in.
Day 2: Feelings scenarios — how do you feel before a test? At a fiesta?
Day 3: Emotion charades with full sentences — 'Está nervioso.'
Day 4: Read a mini-story tracking a character's changing feelings; chart them.
Day 5: Partner check-in interviews; report back — 'Marco está contento.'

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — asking and telling age and birthday
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: 'Tengo nueve años' — Spanish uses tener for age, not ser; age circle practice.
Day 2: Age interviews across the class; tally ages on a chart.
Day 3: '¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños?' — combine with months (week 8).
Day 4: Family ages — 'Mi abuela tiene setenta años' (recycles big numbers).
Day 5: Birthday-graph presentation — read the class data aloud in Spanish.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — presenting a personal poster
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Plan the 'Todo sobre mí' poster — name, age, family, feelings, favorites.
Day 2: Draft sentences using every frame learned so far; teacher conferences.
Day 3: Build the cartel — título, dibujos, final sentences.
Day 4: Rehearse presenting with a partner; practice loud-and-slow delivery.
Day 5: Poster presentations — each student presents; audience asks one question.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — foods the Americas gave the world
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Fruit/vegetable sort with picture cards; add color descriptions.
Day 2: Discover that papas, tomates, maíz, and aguacates all come from the Americas — food origin map.
Day 3: Note LatAm word choices: la papa (not patata), el limón; taste-test day if possible.
Day 4: Write a shopping list of 8 items with quantities.
Day 5: Market-stall game — request items from your list with courtesy phrases.

weeks.topic: Meals & what I like to eat
weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — discussing meals and food preferences
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Three-meals sort; 'En el desayuno como...' frames.
Day 2: Me gusta vs. me encanta — preference interviews about foods.
Day 3: Read a menu from a Latin American restaurant; find familiar foods.
Day 4: Write your dream menu for one day (three meals, drinks).
Day 5: Menu partner-share — compare: '¿Te gusta...?' 'Sí, me encanta.'

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — shopping and bargaining at a mercado
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Video/photo tour of a real mercado; list what's for sale.
Day 2: Price practice — '¿Cuánto cuesta?' 'Cuesta veinte pesos' (recycles numbers).
Day 3: Barato/caro comparisons; learn that friendly bargaining is normal at many mercados.
Day 4: Make stall signs with items and prices.
Day 5: Class mercado — half sell, half buy with play pesos, then switch.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — demonstrating comprehension across all fall topics
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Review stations — greetings, numbers, family, food, weather games.
Day 2: Listening challenge — hear short descriptions, pick the matching picture.
Day 3: Story listen-along using fall vocabulary; answer sí/no questions.
Day 4: Team quiz-show review with buzzer rounds.
Day 5: Self-check day — students mark can-do statements ('Puedo contar hasta 100') and set a goal.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — reading room labels and home descriptions
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: House floor-plan vocabulary; label a big class floor plan.
Day 2: Read short home descriptions, match each to its floor plan.
Day 3: 'Where do you...?' — match activities to rooms (como en el comedor).
Day 4: Draw and label your home's floor plan (casa or apartamento).
Day 5: Home tours — walk a partner through your floor plan in sentences.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — talking about who does which chores
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Chore charades — act out and name each quehacer.
Day 2: 'Yo lavo los platos' — who-does-what interviews with tally chart.
Day 3: Match chores to rooms (recycles week 19).
Day 4: Design a family chore chart in Spanish.
Day 5: Negotiate-the-chores role play — divide a chore list fairly with a partner.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — the plaza at the heart of Latin American towns
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Town-places vocabulary with a map-building activity.
Day 2: Explore the plaza — photos of plazas from Mexico City to Cusco; what happens there?
Day 3: 'Voy al cine' — where-are-you-going mini-dialogues.
Day 4: Compare: does your neighborhood have a plaza-like gathering place?
Day 5: Design-a-town project — draw and label an ideal town with a plaza at its center.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — asking for and giving simple directions
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Direction TPR — turn derecha/izquierda, point aquí/allí.
Day 2: '¿Dónde está el banco?' — answer with está + direction phrases on the town map.
Day 3: Blindfold-free maze — guide a partner across the room with spoken directions.
Day 4: Hidden-treasure map activity — follow written directions to the X.
Day 5: Direction-giving showdown — teams navigate the class town map fastest.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — understanding how people travel
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Transportation review + city transit words (metro, parada, boleto).
Day 2: Listen to 'how I get to school' clips; chart the ways.
Day 3: Mexico City metro map peek — icons help everyone read it!
Day 4: Class survey: how do we get to school? Graph a pie vs. carro vs. autobús.
Day 5: Plan a pretend trip — choose transport, buy a boleto role-play.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — sharing what you like to do
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Hobby pictionary — draw and guess the pasatiempo.
Day 2: 'Me gusta + infinitive' frames — me gusta nadar, me gusta leer.
Day 3: Hobby interviews — find a classmate who shares your hobby.
Day 4: Write a weekend plan: three activities you like to do.
Day 5: Free-time show-and-tell — bring or draw something from your hobby, present in Spanish.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — fútbol and béisbol across Latin America
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Sports vocabulary with action miming; favorite-sport survey.
Day 2: Why fútbol matters across Latin America; béisbol in the Caribbean — mini map study.
Day 3: Sports commentary listening — who ganó, who perdió?
Day 4: Design a team — name, colors, sport, write a team card.
Day 5: Present your equipo; class votes for a friendly award in each category.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — understanding times of day and schedules
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Clock reading — es la una, son las dos... with mini clock manipulatives.
Day 2: Time dictation — hear a time, set your clock.
Day 3: Half-past and quarter hours (y media, y cuarto) for grade 4-5 stretch.
Day 4: Daily schedule match — what time is lunch, recess, Spanish class?
Day 5: Time bingo with student callers.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — narrating your morning routine in order
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Routine TPR sequence — act the morning in order as it's narrated.
Day 2: Sequence cards — put a character's routine in order, narrate with me despierto/me levanto frames.
Day 3: Add times — 'Me despierto a las siete' (recycles week 26).
Day 4: Comic strip — draw your 5-step morning routine with captions.
Day 5: Present your routine comic to a small group.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — talking about the subjects you study
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Subject vocabulary; match each to its classroom objects.
Day 2: Opinion frames — 'Las matemáticas son fáciles/difíciles'; class opinion graph.
Day 3: Read a student's horario from Mexico; find similarities to yours.
Day 4: Build your ideal Friday horario with times (recycles week 26).
Day 5: Schedule interviews — '¿Qué clase tienes a las diez?'

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — habitats and amazing animals (science link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Meet the animals — photos, names, and one fact each.
Day 2: Habitat sort — which animal lives in la selva, las montañas, el desierto?
Day 3: Animal fact cards — read simple Spanish facts, match to the animal.
Day 4: Choose an animal, write 3 sentences (name, habitat, description).
Day 5: Animal expo — present your animal card; class guesses before the reveal.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — maps, countries, and landforms (geography link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Where is Spanish spoken? Color the 21 countries on a blank map.
Day 2: Capital-match game for 6-8 focus countries.
Day 3: Landforms — find el Amazonas, los Andes, dos océanos on the map.
Day 4: Map riddles — 'Este país está entre dos océanos' (recycles entre).
Day 5: Country postcard — pick a country, draw its map and one landform, present it.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — Mexican traditions, food, and music
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Mexico map + flag study — what do the colors and eagle mean?
Day 2: Listen to mariachi; learn where and when it's played.
Day 3: Food tour — tacos, tortillas, and regional dishes (recycles food weeks).
Day 4: Mexican celebrations preview — Día de la Independencia, posadas.
Day 5: Mexico fact-fair — each student shares one learned fact in a Spanish sentence.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Acquiring Information & Diverse Perspectives — the Inca world through Peruvian eyes
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Peru map journey — coast, Andes, Amazon in one country.
Day 2: Machu Picchu virtual visit; what did the Incas build and why?
Day 3: Quechua lives on — millions still speak it alongside Spanish; hear a greeting in both.
Day 4: Andean music listening (la quena) and alpaca textiles — arts of the Andes.
Day 5: 'Postcard from Peru' — write 2-3 Spanish sentences from an imagined visit.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — remembering loved ones with joy
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: What is Día de los Muertos? A joyful remembering, not a scary day — photos and story.
Day 2: Parts of an ofrenda — flowers, photos, velas, favorite foods; why each is placed.
Day 3: Make papel picado; hang a class banner.
Day 4: Compare — how does your family remember loved ones? Respectful sharing circle.
Day 5: Gallery walk of class work; each student names their favorite tradition learned.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Cultural Comparisons — comparing school days across countries
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Watch/read about a school day in Mexico or Colombia; note surprises.
Day 2: Venn diagram — uniformes, horarios, recreo: igual o diferente?
Day 3: Interview prompts — what would you ask a student there? Draft questions.
Day 4: Write 3 comparison sentences using es igual / es diferente.
Day 5: Share comparisons; vote on the most interesting diferencia discovered.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: School & Global Communities — using Spanish to help our neighbors
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Where is Spanish spoken in our own community? Brainstorm and map it.
Day 2: Design a bilingual kindness poster for the school or library.
Day 3: Learn 3 helpful phrases to welcome a Spanish-speaking visitor or new student.
Day 4: Plan a mini service idea (book drive, welcome cards) with Spanish labels.
Day 5: Deliver or display the class project; reflect on using Spanish for real.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: Lifelong Learning — showing growth and setting next-year Spanish goals
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Plan the 'Mi mundo' showcase piece — pick your best topic from the year (family, animals, Peru, routine...).
Day 2: Draft and polish your presentation sentences; teacher conferences.
Day 3: Rehearse with a partner audience; practice projecting to el público.
Day 4: Showcase day — present to families or a buddy class; aplausos for everyone.
Day 5: Reflection + goals — mark end-of-year can-do statements, write one meta for next year, celebrate.
